events.title: Lumboka-Chetambe war
events.summary: The Lumboka-Chetambe war was a military confrontation and a war of resistance by the Ababukusu and the Abatachoni sects of the Abaluhya community against the British Empire in present-day Western Kenya, taking place from 1894 to 1895, just as the British were starting to establish their presence in East Africa.

events.title: The East Africa Rifles are raised
events.summary: The East Africa Rifles was a British Colonial Auxiliary Forces military unit created in 1895 that was later merged into the King's African Rifles in 1902. Based in the East Africa Protectorate but containing troops from across the British Empire, it fought against the Mazrui and the Ogaden people in Jubaland.

events.title: Work begins on the Uganda Railway
events.summary: The Uganda Railway was a metre-gauge railway system and former British state-owned railway company. The line linked the interiors of Uganda and Kenya with the Indian Ocean port of Mombasa in Kenya.

events.title: The Tsavo man-eaters
events.summary: The Tsavo Man-Eaters were a pair of large man-eating male lions in the Tsavo region of Kenya, which were responsible for the deaths of many construction workers on the Kenya-Uganda Railway between March and December 1898. The lion pair was said to have killed dozens of people, with some early estimates reaching over a hundred deaths.

events.title: 1899 famine in central Kenya
events.summary: The famine in central Kenya in 1899 is regarded as a devastating catastrophe in Kenyan history. It spread rapidly from 1898 in the central region of the country around Mount Kenya after several consecutive years of low rainfall.
